# conf-tldr

> Summaries of conference talks. Each has key points with video timestamps, numbers the speakers shared, open gaps, opportunities, and links to slides and open-source projects.

Structured data for every talk: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/data/<series>/<edition>/talks.jsonl

## KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026

- [AI Gateways in Practice: Model Routing, Inference Scheduling, and MCP on Kubernetes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/SerQWvNyI0M.md): Using the Higress gateway, the talk walks through three AI traffic paths on Kubernetes: hosted model providers with fallback, self-hosted models behind Gateway API Inference Extension pools, and agent tool calls over MCP. It compares an endpoint picker embedded in the gateway with an external EPP such as llm-d's, including how each behaves on failure.
- [Agentic AI: Let’s Build a Reference Architecture, Live? Or at Least Try!](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/dOJarSz8FeQ.md): In a CNCF End User Technical Advisory Board session, Ricardo Rocha drew a layered agentic AI reference architecture live from audience input: gateway, orchestration, sandboxing, inference, infrastructure and observability. Attendees named their tools and gaps, mainly caller identity, data privacy and the lack of a shared agent harness, and were asked to submit their own reference architectures.
- [Agentic Inference at Scale](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/7gvpGm3GCB4.md): Agent sessions send about 100 tokens in for every token out, so serving them well is about never recomputing context. llm-d 1.0 packages cache-aware routing, offloading and disaggregation, adds day-2 operations, and a new SIG is moving scheduling from single requests to whole sessions.
- [Agents Fail. Workflows Recover. Durable Agent Orchestration with Cadence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/n8t6AblQUMY.md): Uber's Cadence team shows how wrapping model and tool calls as Cadence activities lets an agent resume after rate limits or worker crashes instead of starting over. Uber's Agent Executor Service already runs hundreds of thousands of agentic workflows on Cadence, and its execution history pointed straight at the cause of most timeouts.
- [Agents on the Platform: Four Perspectives on the Conversation We're Already Having in Private](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/oWFO88oAHOY.md): A panel with platform, OpenTelemetry, security and inference perspectives discusses what platform teams must provide to run agents: sandboxing, identity, observability and inference routing. The shared advice is to rely on maturing community projects, treat agents as adversarial, instrument them from within, and learn the stack hands-on before rushing.
- [Beyond Model Serving: Running Production LLMs on Kubernetes with KServe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/WPukEewRCOI.md): KServe maintainers explain LLMInferenceService, a separate API from InferenceService that wraps llm-d, vLLM and Gateway API Inference Extension routing so one resource can describe single-node, multi-node and prefill/decode-disaggregated deployments. They then walk through production patterns: cache-aware routing, timeouts, queue-based autoscaling, cold-start reduction, rollouts and LoRA adapters.
- [Beyond the Cluster Boundary: Sharing GPUs at Scale](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/9EQCSHWCN6Y.md): Snap pooled its reserved GPUs into capacity-pool clusters and lets workloads in thousands of customer clusters reach them through virtual nodes built on Virtual Kubelet, with Kueue gating access and handling borrowing and preemption. Average reservation occupancy in its largest region rose from under 50% to over 90%, saving tens of millions of dollars a year.
- [Cache Me If You Can: LLM Inference with llm-d (with fun drawings)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/ixmKvIejJv4.md): A step-by-step tour of llm-d: how the endpoint picker filters, scores and picks a pod, and where prefix-aware routing, KV offloading and prefill/decode disaggregation fit. Most of the talk is a practical guide to flow control: saturation detectors, fairness policies and priority holdback.
- [Choose Your Own Adventure: The Saga of Serving LLM Inference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/gNAANhDs5cc.md): The audience voted on three vLLM serving choices (quantization, sharding versus replication, speculative decoding) and the speakers deployed that configuration and its opposite side by side under load. The audience's full-precision, sharded, speculative setup was more accurate but served fewer requests, and the speakers' advice is to run experiments, not pick in advance.
- [Clueless About The Cost of AI Model Usage? OpenCost+llm-d = first of a kind inference cost tracking](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/v0qNmkJSJ8A.md): OpenCost now reads llm-d and vLLM token metrics and combines them with provider pricing and DCGM data to report cost per model and per token. A live demo on an IBM research cluster compares allocation and usage cost to expose idle models, and the roadmap targets GPU usage-based allocation, time slicing and richer idle detection.
- [Composing Inference on Kubernetes: Gateway, Schedule, Serve, Observe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/02tyAmdoleQ.md): Production inference should be built from open, swappable layers: accelerators, scheduling, gateway, serving and observability. The test is whether you can swap one layer, such as vLLM for SGLang or one endpoint picker for another, without the others noticing.
- [Deep Dive Into the DRA Driver for NVIDIA GPUs: What Works Today, What’s Coming and Why It Matters](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/vYDpOV7IvEc.md): NVIDIA's DRA driver for GPUs already handles time-slicing, MPS, MIG, VM passthrough, health-based device taints and multi-node NVLink through compute domains. The next release adds cross-namespace GPU sharing, several compute-domain pods per node, an always-on IMEX daemon set and beta graduation of most driver features.
- [Demystifying Upgrades for Stateful, Dormant AI Agents: Unleashing Seamless Updates in Dynamic Sandboxes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/eQoE0J6xnkA.md): Cloud-hosted agent sandboxes need near-daily harness and CVE updates, but their state (sessions, skills, installed tools) sits in the container's writable layer and is lost on restart. OpenKruise Agents offers upgrade paths for warm pools, sandbox claims, and running or paused sandboxes, plus a session-aware sandbox service for fleet-level rollouts.
- [DisaggregatedSet Meets Multi-EPP: Coordinating llm-d at Scale in production](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/pVKqTxIDZcw.md): Mistral runs llm-d in production and contributed two pieces back: DisaggregatedSet, which manages prefill and decode as one unit inside LeaderWorkerSet, and a cross-replica syncer that lets several endpoint pickers share state so routing scales out.
- [Dropping LLM Inference Cost by Two-Thirds with Open Weights and Kubernetes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/_jb3uLrTa3s.md): An AWS solutions architect replaced a proprietary LLM API in a multi-label classification pipeline with a QLoRA-fine-tuned Qwen3 8B model served by vLLM on EKS, raising exact-match accuracy from 56% to 91% at one-third of the cost. Quantization, prefix caching and speculative decoding raised per-GPU throughput, but surges exposed slow GPU capacity, which was fixed with smaller and pre-baked images and headroom.
- [Fireside Chat: Future of Kubernetes and Agents with Tim Hockin and Kelsey Hightower](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/f3HsQwhIAnE.md): Savannah Peterson hosts Tim Hockin and Kelsey Hightower on why agents need a different platform layer: they are untrusted, mostly idle and single-tenant, which normal Kubernetes patterns serve with poor startup times or poor utilization. They frame Agent Substrate as Kubernetes extended for a new workload, urge teams to check they need an agent at all, and name delegated identity and permission scoping as open problems.
- [Follow the GPUs: How a Regulated Fortune 100 Serves Customers When No Single Cloud Has Enough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/71NwaH0y5OM.md): GEICO runs a hybrid cloud fabric (flat L3 network, identical clusters, SPIFFE/SPIRE identity, Istio and Cilium) that makes moving a workload between Azure and AWS just a redeploy. They built a probe tool that measured GPU availability across providers for four weeks and found multi-region helps only for scarce SKUs, and propose a capacity booking agent since autoscalers never buy capacity.
- [Frameworkless ML Serving: Scaling to Thousands of Models with KEDA, Pub/Sub, and Native K8s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/fAZ-8I62m5s.md): Isomorphic Labs moved from Vertex AI to Ray Serve to a framework-free platform where every model is a stateless Kubernetes Deployment pulling from its own Pub/Sub queue behind a stateless gateway. KEDA scales workers to zero, Kubernetes priority and preemption put interactive traffic ahead of batch, and narrow interfaces let them swap storage backends live.
- [From GPU to Fleet. The llm-d KV Cache Hierarchy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/gC7GfYxrZgI.md): Agent traffic is long input and short output, so reusing KV cache matters more than raw GPU speed. llm-d and vLLM now tier KV cache from GPU to CPU to shared storage and route requests to where the cache already lives.
- [From Laptop to Cluster: The Agentic AI Inner Loop on Kubernetes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/KCBdIFOmzEU.md): Using a live audience race game run by an AI race director, the speaker shows an agentic Java app built with Quarkus and LangChain4j that exposes MCP tools and calls sub-agents over A2A. He argues agents are mostly ordinary code: develop locally with hot reload and a dev UI, add evals, then ship to Kubernetes with configuration changes and standard security and health patterns.
- [From Proxy to Platform: Building a Multi-Tenant AI Gateway](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/YaEXW7f9Dr0.md): Adobe built a shared, multi-tenant LLM gateway on LiteLLM, with its own control plane (console) for self-service model onboarding, fallbacks, budgets and logs. The talk walks through the stages from shared keys to team tenants, agent-driven usage and platform guarantees, and where they go next.
- [Governing and Scaling Agents in Heterogeneous Environments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/wB5-lqrDCbw.md): Antonio Ojea and Tomás Tormo present Agent Mesh, a network for agents running on Kubernetes, laptops, VMs and serverless, built on a libp2p peer-to-peer data plane with Kademlia discovery. Policy travels with each node as signed, attenuable Biscuit tokens minted at enrollment, and a live hospital demo shows label-based rules keeping EU data in the EU.
- [Groundhog Pod: Scaling AI Inference with Kata Pod Snapshots](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/4FzdSErl41M.md): Microsoft extended Kata Containers and Cloud Hypervisor to snapshot a whole pod VM, including GPU state captured with CUDA checkpoint, after the model is loaded. Restoring from the snapshot cut a demo inference pod's time to first response from about 34 seconds to about 11.
- [Inside the Inference Load Balancer: Proxy/Controller Patterns for LLM Serving on Kubernetes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/wNJVJ8PhFO0.md): OpenAI's inference load balancer picks a GPU engine for every request across clusters and regions. A global control plane computes routing weights from demand, capacity and latency profiles; fast local data planes apply them, with penalties, retry caps and load shedding for protection.
- [Just Keep Swimming: Benchmarking OSS Agent Memory on Kubernetes with OpenTelemetry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/LSFk3nqozcY.md): Henrik Rexed benchmarks five open-source agent memory servers on kagent with a shared generic MCP layer and OpenTelemetry instrumentation he contributed upstream. Memory helps only when recall is precise: embedding and graph approaches did best for SRE investigations, a key-based store did best for context-rich coding crews, and MemPalace and Zep were the most consistent overall.
- [Kubernetes Solutions for Agent-Shaped Problems](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/G-8hPDtRVB8.md): Tim Hockin and Dmitry Berkovich explain why the obvious pod-per-agent-session pattern on Kubernetes gives slow starts and poor utilization, and how Agent Substrate fixes it with secure-by-default sandboxes, near-zero cost for idle agents and fast wake from layered snapshots. The long Q&A covers the policy enforcement point, snapshot invalidation and missing pieces such as autoscaling and automatic suspend.
- [Least-Privilege by Default: Standardizing Identity-Aware AI Agent Access into a Golden Path](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/4T8Sy76WppM.md): Least privilege for an agent acting on a user's behalf means every call may do only what both the user and the agent are allowed to do. Hitachi's design builds seven rules into a platform golden path using Keycloak token exchange, SPIFFE/SPIRE attestation, attribute-based policy and Backstage templates, so teams only declare and approve.
- [Lessons Learned Sandboxing Agents with kagent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/rAyt198OTFA.md): Solo.io engineers tried a pod per agent, Anthropic's sandbox runtime, Agent Sandbox and NVIDIA OpenShell, and found each solved only part of the problem, so they joined Google's Agent Substrate and rebuilt kagent 1.0 on it. Their main lessons: isolation is table stakes, and the hard parts are suspend and resume, keeping all controls outside the agent, identity that follows the session, and treating snapshots as sensitive data.
- [Many Clusters, One GPU Pool: Locality-Aware Scheduling and Data Delivery With Kueue and Dragonfly](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/kHbLvCbxslg.md): Roblox joined five Kubernetes clusters across three AWS regions and its own data center into one GPU pool with MultiKueue, a custom external dispatcher and tiered quotas. Dragonfly P2P caching in each cluster turned repeated cross-region S3 reads into local and peer reads for training data and model weights.
- [New Traffic, New Rules: Standardizing AI-Aware Networking in Kubernetes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/kwJTUGK4FPM.md): The Kubernetes AI Gateway Working Group presents its proposals for AI-aware traffic in Gateway API: pre-routing payload processing, a Backend resource, an endpoint selector, gateway routability and multi-stage routes. The goal is one standard set of APIs so different routers stop building their own body parsing, egress and inference orchestration.
- [Observability for LLM Inference on Kubernetes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/4T2887KV_WM.md): With frontier APIs you only see the client side, but self-hosting on Kubernetes lets you observe every layer from the GPU up to the user response. The speakers instrument an OCR app on KServe, vLLM and llm-d with OpenTelemetry and correlate metrics, traces and logs in Grafana to find wasted tokens and misleading GPU utilization.
- [One Workload to Rule Them All: Workload Aware Scheduling for Distributed AI Training on Kubernetes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/3O1MewPx8oA.md): Kubernetes now has Workload, PodGroup and composite PodGroup APIs so kube-scheduler can gang-schedule, preempt and place a whole distributed job instead of single pods. Kubeflow Trainer builds these into TrainJob runtimes so platform admins set gang and topology rules while scientists only write a training function.
- [Platform-First AI Agent Security: Zero-Trust Patterns for Kubernetes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/rTsCnDDMiik.md): Carlos Santana argues platform teams should treat AI agents as untrusted tenants and layer identity, policy and isolation around them using CNCF projects. He shows KRO compositions that stamp out agent workloads, egress policies and Agent Substrate worker pools per namespace, plus Agent Sandbox warm pools, OpenShell with Cedar policies, and credential proxies.
- [Pods Are Not Enough for AI Agents, Meet Agent-substrate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/gzga1kARmxI.md): Christian Posta argues that agents break microservice assumptions: they run unknown code, hold state and sit idle, so a session per pod overloads Kubernetes. Agent Substrate decouples actors from worker pods, snapshots idle actors to storage, wakes them on request, and forces all egress through policy with credential injection; kagent supplies the agent-aware layer on top.
- [Quota Isn't Enough: Topology Aware Scheduling on Modern GPU Clusters](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/_njXLk28JT0.md): On NVL72 racks the NVLink domain is the whole rack, and leaving it drops bandwidth 18x, so having GPU quota no longer means a job will run fast or start at all. The speakers explain Kueue Topology Aware Scheduling and production lessons on test pods, slice sizing, node hot swap, preemption tickets, fragmentation and hero workloads.
- [Reduce vLLM Pod Cold Starts with KServe Kernel Caching](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/v1o70EZXaZY.md): Even with model weights cached, each new vLLM pod recompiles its GPU kernels. KServe now captures those compiled artifacts, publishes them as signed OCI images, and lets new pods reuse them, cutting compile time from about 35 seconds to about 1 second in their tests.
- [Running Secure Agents at Scale](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/gDLFk6_To34.md): Adobe Experience Manager runs a few thousand single-tenant agents that import and redesign customer websites, each needing a sandboxed Playwright browser. After comparing Agent Sandbox, OpenShell, Substrate and others, Adobe chose Agent Sandbox with warm pools because its agents run long sessions rather than short bursts.
- [Securing the Agentic Future: Distributing LLM Weights and Sandboxed AI Agents via Harbor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/yJ7i1K488lg.md): An AI agent ships as two things, model weights and the sandbox it acts in, and today neither goes through the supply chain teams already use for container images. The talk shows Harbor storing weights as ModelPack OCI artifacts and agent images with a sandbox permission descriptor, so both get the same scanning, signing, replication and admission policy.
- [Seeing Inside LLM Inference: Observability and Cost Visibility for llm-d on Kubernetes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/68m9PQsSvyE.md): The llm-d observability and router SIG leads show end-to-end tracing of a request through the gateway, endpoint picker, KV cache lookup and prefill/decode pods, and use metric-to-trace-to-log correlation to find a bad scorer weight behind a TTFT regression. They then describe combining llm-d metrics with OpenCost to compute per-token, per-tenant cost, which is early work that is already upstream.
- [Simulate, Evolve, Validate, Ship: AI-Discovered Algorithms for LLM Serving Stacks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/UooQd0QU7go.md): IBM Research uses a CPU-based simulator of llm-d and vLLM plus an agentic harness to discover serving policies, then validates the winners on GPUs and upstreams them to llm-d. The loop has produced admission control, flow control and LoRA routing plugins for the llm-d router.
- [The Agent Has Entered the Cluster: AI Auth 101 for Kubernetes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/08nLTg2YDOI.md): A user's identity usually stops at the agent, so downstream tools and the Kubernetes API act with their own broad service-account permissions. The speakers assess a diagnostic agent by identity, delegation and scoped authority, then fix it with least-privilege RBAC, tool policies in agentgateway and a forwarded user token.
- [The Latest in GPU, TPU, NIC and Other Device Support - WG Device Management](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/ohw9hntgNCU.md): WG Device Management reviewed what Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) shipped in Kubernetes 1.37 and what is landing in 1.38, from device taints and extended-resource compatibility to partitionable devices and CPU allocation through DRA. Next up are DRA preemption, gang-aware preemption, richer hardware models and attaching GPUs to running pods.
- [The Scheduling Stack: Real-World Lessons from Anthropic, Anyscale, Google, and CERN](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/t-r-my2ngZ8.md): Big AI users still outgrow the default Kubernetes scheduler, so upstream is turning the scheduling stack into pluggable parts. The hard problems now are fragmentation, multi-cluster onboarding and failures, not raw node count.
- [The Seams Are the Trap: Agent Fleets from CNCF Parts You Already Have](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/zrqy2rulX4M.md): IBM speakers built a headless agent fleet from existing CNCF parts: KEDA scales agent runners from Kafka lag, CloudEvents carry the tasks, and a small Python glue layer bridges HTTP and Kafka. Events are signed and kept in order, so the Kafka log doubles as a verifiable audit trail, while agent identity with SPIFFE/SPIRE is still unsolved.
- [Who Ran Up the Inference Bill? AI Traffic Control with KServe and Gateway API Inference Extensions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/ymgukAwlT8c.md): A beginner-level talk on attributing and controlling inference spend by putting an AI-aware gateway in front of KServe models. A live demo on kind uses agentgateway with the Gateway API Inference Extension to log tokens per team, enforce per-team token budgets, block sensitive data and fail over to a cloud LLM.
- [Why Are You Still Wasting Whole GPUs? Hardware-Level Sharing, Scheduled with DRA](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/qGvckRV9AwU.md): A Pulumi solutions architect describes building a self-hosted inference platform for a European customer that splits GPUs into NVIDIA MIG slices and schedules them with Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA). MIG gives the isolation time-slicing lacks, and DRA lets workloads ask for slices by attributes, but quotas, large models and chargeback remain open.
- [Your Peers Are Struggling With LLM Inference on Kubernetes Too. Here's What the Data Says](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/HMcnjNuwjAY.md): Using an Akamai-commissioned survey of 200 practitioners running AI in production, plus CNCF, Forrester and Cast AI data, the speakers show that most teams struggle with latency at peak, GPU capacity and routing. They map the failure points across scheduling, scaling, networking and ownership, and close with five steps to production inference on Kubernetes.
- [Zero-Gap GPU Execution: Building Secure, Pre-Warmed Pod Runtimes for High-Velocity AI Agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/j0kV0TekF3c.md): LinkedIn built Firepool, a broker that keeps warm GPU pods ready so agents and RL loops running on CPU nodes can launch GPU jobs without Kubernetes pod startup in the critical path. Its zero-gap mode uses HAMi and Volcano to park standby pods on a busy GPU so the next job takes over the card the moment the current one ends.
- [llm-d 1.0 Production-Grade Inference for Cloud-Native AI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avinashdesireddy/conf-tldr/main/events/kubecon/na-2026/talks/O4Et_Xk2Cg4.md): llm-d 1.0 marks the core stack as production-ready: KV-aware routing, prefill/decode disaggregation, KV offloading and flow control, behind a stable v1 API. IBM ran it on 500+ H100s for an internal agentic workload, and a demo shows throughput nearly doubling on the same hardware.
